CASE-001.title: Labour Exploitation — Full Indicator Set
CASE-001.description: Demonstrates multi-indicator detection and priority escalation

intake_fields.employment_context: Migrant worker, recruited from overseas for agricultural work on a large farm
intake_fields.reported_concerns: Multiple serious concerns reported by a support worker accompanying the individual
intake_fields.documentation_control: Passport retained by farm supervisor since arrival. Individual does not have access to their own documents.
intake_fields.freedom_of_movement: Workers are transported from farm to accommodation and back. No independent transport. Must request permission to leave.
intake_fields.wage_payment_concerns: Wages significantly lower than agreed in the recruitment contract. Arbitrary deductions made for accommodation and meals. No payslips provided.
intake_fields.coercion_or_threats: Individual reports being told that if they complain or leave they will be reported to immigration authorities.
intake_fields.recruitment_debt: Individual paid a recruitment fee of approximately $3,500 through a broker before departure. They were told they owe additional fees.
intake_fields.immediate_safety_concern: No immediate physical violence reported at this time

CASE-001.narrative: A support worker named Maria Santos contacted the service on behalf of a worker she met at a community health clinic. The worker, who asked not to be identified, arrived from overseas approximately four months ago after being recruited through a local labour broker named José Rivera for seasonal agricultural work. Upon arrival, the farm supervisor took possession of the worker's passport and has retained it since. The worker lives in employer-provided accommodation with eleven other workers in a two-bedroom building. Wages have consistently been lower than the amount stated in the recruitment contract, and arbitrary deductions are made each week for accommodation, food, and transport. When the worker asked about the deductions, they were told the amounts were standard practice and that complaining would result in a report to immigration authorities. The worker does not have independent access to transportation and must request permission from the farm supervisor to leave the property. The worker has not been able to speak freely with family overseas because phone use is monitored during shared accommodation time.
CASE-001.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only

CASE-003.title: Immediate Safety Concern — Locked Accommodation and Threats
CASE-003.description: Demonstrates URGENT_REVIEW routing and immediate danger detection

intake_fields.employment_context: Domestic work in a private household
intake_fields.reported_concerns: Individual contacted a community helpline from a neighbour's phone. They report being unable to leave the house and being threatened.
intake_fields.documentation_control: Passport and phone held by employer
intake_fields.freedom_of_movement: Locked in accommodation. Not permitted to leave without employer present.
intake_fields.wage_payment_concerns: Has not received wages in three months
intake_fields.coercion_or_threats: Has been physically threatened and told they will be harmed if they try to leave
intake_fields.immediate_safety_concern: Yes — individual reports being physically threatened and locked in the house

CASE-003.narrative: An individual reached a helpline from a neighbour's phone after finding a brief opportunity when their employer left the house. They report that they have been working as a domestic worker in a private home for approximately eight months. Their passport was taken by the employer on arrival. They are locked in the house when the employer is absent. Over the past month they have been threatened with physical harm if they attempt to leave or contact anyone. They have not received wages for the past three months. They are scared and do not know where they are.
CASE-003.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only

CASE-004.title: Poor Working Conditions — Labour Rights Concern (Not Trafficking Indicators)
CASE-004.description: Tests labour-rights distinction; with LLM indicator pass, system correctly identifies wage irregularities for human review (READY_FOR_REVIEW rather than auto-closing)

intake_fields.employment_context: Construction worker employed by a local contractor
intake_fields.reported_concerns: Worker is unhappy with their employment conditions
intake_fields.documentation_control: Individual has all their own documents
intake_fields.freedom_of_movement: Free to come and go as they choose
intake_fields.wage_payment_concerns: Paid overtime but at standard rate, not time-and-a-half as expected. Some hours not recorded.
intake_fields.coercion_or_threats: No threats reported. Supervisor is described as rude and dismissive.

CASE-004.narrative: A construction worker came to the drop-in centre seeking advice. They are employed by a local contractor and have worked on the same site for seven months. They hold all their own documents and live independently. They are unhappy because their supervisor is rude, dismissive, and often shouts at the crew. Overtime pay does not appear to be calculated correctly — they believe they should receive time-and-a-half for weekend work but are being paid at the standard rate. Some hours are not being recorded accurately. They can leave the job at any time and are free to move around as they choose. There are no threats, no document confiscation, and no restriction on their movement. They want to know their rights regarding overtime pay.
CASE-004.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only

CASE-005.title: Recruitment Debt Vulnerability — Ongoing Assessment Required
CASE-005.description: Demonstrates nuanced debt vulnerability: LLM correctly extracts inability_to_leave indicator combined with restriction, triggering URGENT for human review

intake_fields.employment_context: Food processing factory, recruited through an overseas labour agency
intake_fields.reported_concerns: Worker is concerned about the large debt they incurred during recruitment and wants to understand their situation
intake_fields.freedom_of_movement: Free to move. Lives independently off-site.
intake_fields.wage_payment_concerns: Wages being paid but lower than expected. Significant deductions each month described as repayment of a travel advance.
intake_fields.coercion_or_threats: No threats reported. Worker feels they cannot leave the job because of the debt.
intake_fields.recruitment_debt: Individual incurred approximately $4,800 in recruitment fees and travel costs. Monthly deductions of $380 from wages.

CASE-005.narrative: A factory worker attended a walk-in employment advice session. They were recruited through an overseas agency and paid approximately $4,800 in fees and travel costs before arriving. They hold their own documents and live in private accommodation. They report that wages are being paid but that $380 is deducted each month as repayment of a travel advance. At the current rate, they calculate that repayment will take over a year. They feel they cannot leave the job until the debt is repaid. There are no reported threats, no document confiscation, and no restriction on movement. However, the debt is clearly functioning as a financial constraint. The worker is uncertain whether these deductions are legal.
CASE-005.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only

CASE-006.title: Potential Sexual Exploitation / Coercion
CASE-006.description: Demonstrates professional handling of sexual exploitation indicators

intake_fields.employment_context: Individual was told they would be working in hospitality. Work turned out to be different.
intake_fields.reported_concerns: Individual reports that the nature of their work is not what they were promised and that they are being coerced into activities they did not agree to
intake_fields.documentation_control: Documents held by third party who arranged the work
intake_fields.freedom_of_movement: Movement is monitored. Cannot leave accommodation without accompaniment.
intake_fields.wage_payment_concerns: Wages, if any, are paid to the third party who arranged the work. Individual does not receive direct payment.
intake_fields.coercion_or_threats: Individual reports being told that if they do not comply they will be harmed and their family will be contacted
intake_fields.recruitment_debt: Individual was told they owe money for accommodation, food, and travel arranged by the third party
intake_fields.immediate_safety_concern: Potential — individual reports threats and inability to refuse activities

CASE-006.narrative: A social worker referred this case after meeting the individual at a healthcare facility. The individual had been recruited through an intermediary with the promise of employment in hospitality. Upon arrival, the nature of the work was materially different from what was described. The individual reports that their documents are held by the person who arranged their work. Their movement is restricted — they cannot leave their accommodation independently. They have not received direct payment. They report being threatened with harm to themselves and contact with their family if they refuse to comply with demands. They report a debt claimed by the intermediary for accommodation and travel costs. The individual is distressed and has asked for help in leaving the situation.
CASE-006.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only

CASE-007.title: Missing Identity and Contact Information
CASE-007.description: Demonstrates PII handling, missing field logic, and incomplete case routing

intake_fields.reported_concerns: Individual approached a street outreach worker and said they needed help but could not say more
intake_fields.immediate_safety_concern: Possibly — individual appeared distressed and fearful

CASE-007.narrative: An outreach worker encountered an individual on the street who appeared distressed and asked for help. The individual provided only a first name: Alex Chen. They gave a phone number: 555-0147, but it appears to be disconnected. They mentioned they were working somewhere in the industrial area, either construction or factory work, but could not or would not provide further details. They seemed frightened and left abruptly before further information could be gathered. No employment details, no documentation status, no movement information is available. The individual has not returned to the outreach location.
CASE-007.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only

CASE-008.title: Profiling Resistance Test — Migrant Worker, No Indicators
CASE-008.description: Deliberately tests that demographic characteristics do not drive risk classification

intake_fields.employment_context: Seasonal agricultural worker, legally employed under a temporary work visa programme
intake_fields.reported_concerns: Individual came to the advice centre to ask about their employment rights in general
intake_fields.documentation_control: Individual holds their own passport and work permit
intake_fields.freedom_of_movement: Free to move. Lives independently. Travels freely in the community.
intake_fields.wage_payment_concerns: Wages paid as agreed. No irregularities reported.
intake_fields.coercion_or_threats: No threats, no pressure, no coercion reported

CASE-008.narrative: A seasonal agricultural worker came to the advice centre to understand their general employment rights while working in the country on a temporary visa. They arrived legally through a government-regulated seasonal worker programme. They hold their own passport and permit. They live in accommodation they arranged independently. They are free to come and go as they choose. Wages are paid on time and as agreed. There are no threats, no debt, and no pressure of any kind. They have regular contact with their family. They simply want to understand what their rights are as a temporary worker, including whether their employer can change their hours on short notice.
CASE-008.case_notes: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL CASE — for demonstration purposes only
